_README: Single source of truth for CV content. cv.html (the 2-page master) and the CV tailor both draw from here. The Cloudflare Worker verifies every bullet it emits against the strings in this file, so nothing reaches a page that isn't approved here. Add a variant here before the tailor can ever use it.

positioning.thesis: My expertise is behavioural and market analysis grounded in statistical method. Give me any sector and I'll learn it fast and make it legible — I've already done it across five unrelated domains.
positioning.capabilityTagline: I answer "why do people do this?" with statistical rigour — across markets, products, and organisations — and turn the answer into something a room can act on.
positioning.methodsLine: Behavioural investigation — designing research and experiments to explain why people, users, and markets behave as they do, and translating findings into decisions.

summaries.master: Analytics strategist and behavioural researcher with 6+ years building data infrastructure, governance, and insight functions for global organisations — most recently owning BI delivery for a newly created talent intelligence function at Publicis Groupe. Proven track record standardising practices across large divisions and translating complex data into strategic insight for audiences ranging from C-suite to entry-level staff. Academically specialised in behavioural economics (MSc) and marketing science (BSc). Targeting analytics leadership, behavioural insight, or research roles where human-centred data shapes product or policy decisions.
summaries.trackA: Behavioural and market analyst with 6+ years applying statistical method to unfamiliar domains — telecom, QSR, retail, media, and workforce — and making each legible to decision-makers. My expertise is the science of understanding markets and behaviour, not any single sector: I arrive without predefined scope, learn the domain fast, find what's actually happening, and deliver something a room can act on. Formally grounded in behavioural economics (MSc, City St George's) and marketing science (BSc), with the technical range to build whatever infrastructure the analysis requires.
summaries.trackB: Applied behavioural researcher with 6+ years designing and executing quantitative studies under real organisational constraints, anchored by a first-class MSc dissertation applying multivariate methods to 11,249 cross-cultural respondents. My domain is method and human behaviour, not a sector — I've applied the same statistical toolkit across five unrelated industries, learning each quickly and translating rigorous analysis into decisions non-specialists can act on. Comfortable across the full pipeline: instrument and experimental design, imputation and construct reduction, regression and interaction modelling, and honest reporting of what a model can and can't support.

dissertation.title: MSc Dissertation — Social Capital & Life Satisfaction: A Cross-Cultural Analysis
dissertation.institution: City St. George's, University of London
dissertation.body: Applied an underused ISSP 2017 instrument to test social capital as multi-dimensional across five national contexts. Methods: PCA construct reduction, MICE imputation (country-grouped), pooled OLS with interaction terms, LSmeans with Tukey correction, VIF and AIC/BIC model comparison. Finding: trust in fairness was the only universal cross-cultural predictor of life satisfaction; absolute income showed no significant effect, though subjective financial strain did.
dissertation.bodyShort: Applied an underused ISSP 2017 instrument to test social capital as multi-dimensional across five national contexts, using PCA construct reduction, MICE imputation, and pooled OLS with interaction terms. Trust in fairness was the only universal cross-cultural predictor of life satisfaction; absolute income showed no significant effect.
